summary: This Wikipedia-derived note introduces the list of kings and queens of the Kingdom of England, starting with Alfred the Great of Wessex and the House of Wessex, the first unbroken line to rule the whole of England. It ends with Queen Anne, the last monarch of a distinct English kingdom, after which the list is continued in List of British monarchs. The note also gives a table entry for Mary I (nicknamed Bloody Mary) and her husband Philip II of Spain, with their reigns, births, marriages, deaths and claims to the throne.
one_line: A list of English monarchs from Alfred the Great to Queen Anne, with a table covering Mary I and her husband Philip II of Spain.
key_facts: Mary I reigned as English monarch from 19 July 1553 to 17 November 1558, a total of 5 years and 122 days.
Mary I was born on 18 February 1516 at Greenwich Palace.
Mary I was the daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon.
Mary I married Philip II of Spain at Winchester Cathedral on 25 July 1554.
Mary I died on 17 November 1558 at St James's Palace, aged 42.
Mary I's claim to the throne is listed as the Third Succession Act.
Philip reigned as husband of Mary I from 25 July 1554 to 17 November 1558, a total of 4 years and 116 days.
Philip II of Spain was born on 21 May 1527 in Valladolid.
Philip was the son of Charles V of the Holy Roman Empire and Isabella of Portugal.
Philip had 3 other marriages and 7 children, and died on 13 September 1598 at El Escorial, aged 71.
Philip's claim is listed as the Act for the Marriage of Queen Mary to Philip of Spain.
The list begins with Alfred the Great, King of Wessex, who styled himself King of the Anglo-Saxons.
The House of Wessex was the first unbroken line of kings to rule the whole of England.
Queen Anne was the last monarch of a distinct kingdom of England, after England merged with Scotland in 1707 to form a union and she became Queen of Great Britain.
